title: Time scale conversion
summary: How an instant enters the model, is stored on one uniform scale, and is read back on any supported scale.

nodes.label: Calendar fields or an MJD, with a scale
nodes.summary: The caller states which scale the number is on. A calendar date is also accepted.

nodes.label: Fields a valid date?
nodes.summary: The month and day must exist in that year, including the leap year rule.

nodes.label: Rejected
nodes.summary: The fields do not form a valid calendar date, or the request is outside the leap second table.

nodes.label: Convert to a day number
nodes.summary: A calendar date becomes a Modified Julian Date on the stated scale.

nodes.label: Which scale?
nodes.summary: TAI, TT, and GPS convert by a constant offset; UTC converts through the leap second table.

nodes.label: Apply the constant offset
nodes.summary: TT minus TAI is 32.184 seconds and TAI minus GPS is 19 seconds.

nodes.label: Look up the leap second offset
nodes.summary: Search the embedded table for the interval that contains the instant.

nodes.label: Covered by the table?
nodes.summary: The table starts at the beginning of 1972.

nodes.label: Epoch on the TAI scale
nodes.summary: The instant is stored as a Modified Julian Date on TAI, so the difference between two instants is exact elapsed time.

nodes.label: Read back on the requested scale
nodes.summary: The inverse of the entry conversion, producing an MJD and a calendar value.

nodes.label: MJD and calendar on every scale
nodes.summary: The result reports UTC, TAI, TT, and GPS together with the offset at that instant.
